operation_details.item: The user uses MongoDB for one of the storage layers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How’s the storage-layer work going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. Postgres is still handling the primary database, and Redis is covering caching.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. Are you using anything else for a specific workload?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, I use MongoDB for one of the storage layers. It fits that data better than forcing everything into Postgres.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Is that choice documented with the rest of the architecture?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, the storage choices are listed in the system design doc.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good place to keep the tradeoffs visible when someone revisits the design.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I’d rather keep the architecture practical than make every component follow the same pattern.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only that I use MongoDB, while keeping the Postgres, Redis, and system-design details.
